column2776: source:["# 7. Model Architecture: Residual Dual-Stream Network\n"
column2778: To capture both structural anomalies and semantic deception in phishing URLs, the model uses the same architecture as the reference notebook `url-cnntrans.ipynb` and `src/inference/network.py`: a residual multi-scale 1D-CNN over characters and a 2-layer, 8-head Transformer encoder over BPE subwords.\n
column2781: The character stream extracts localized URL structure such as typosquatting, suspicious n-grams, encoded payloads, and separator patterns.\n
column2782: * **Input & Regularization:** Characters are mapped into a 64-dimensional embedding space. `SpatialDropout1D(p=0.2)` drops complete feature channels to reduce reliance on a single memorized character pattern.\n
column2783: * **Parallel Convolutional Bank:** Five parallel 1D convolution paths use kernel sizes `[2, 3, 4, 5, 7]`. Each path starts with `Conv1d -> BatchNorm1d -> GELU`, then adds one residual convolution block. The residual connection deepens the CNN path while preserving gradient flow.\n
column2784: * **Pooling & Projection:** Each convolution path is adaptively max-pooled, concatenated, and projected into the 256-dimensional shared feature space as `h_char`. The unpooled CNN map is also projected into the 128-dimensional Transformer space to serve as cross-attention keys and values.\n
column2787: The word stream processes BPE subwords to model URL vocabulary and longer-range token relationships.\n
column2788: * **Input Representation:** BPE tokens are mapped to a 128-dimensional embedding space. Learned absolute positional embeddings support `MAX_LEN_WORD` tokens, and a learnable `[CLS]` token is prepended.\n
column2789: * **Self-Attention Encoder:** The sequence is processed by a lightweight 2-layer Transformer encoder with 8 attention heads (`nhead=8`) and a feed-forward dimension of 256.\n
column2790: * **Word-Only Auxiliary Signal:** Before cross-attention injection, the `[CLS]` state is projected to `h_word_raw` and used by the auxiliary word head. This keeps branch-level word supervision focused on the Transformer/BPE stream.\n
column2792: ### 7.3. Scaled Cross-Attention Injection, Fusion, and Auxiliary Training\n
column2793: After self-attention, the Transformer sequence queries the CNN feature map. The cross-attention output is multiplied by a learnable scalar `cross_attn_scale` initialized to `0.10` before being added back through a residual path and LayerNorm. This lets the model use CNN context without forcing the word branch to depend on it too early.\n
column2794: * **Post-Injection Word Representation:** The updated `[CLS]` token is projected to `h_word` for final fusion.\n
column2795: * **Balanced Softmax Fusion:** A zero-initialized softmax gate computes two weights from `[h_char, h_word]` and forms `h_fused = g_cnn * h_char + g_word * h_word`. The zero initialization starts both branches balanced.\n
column2796: * **Auxiliary Supervision:** The CNN auxiliary head uses `h_char`; the word auxiliary head uses `h_word_raw`. Auxiliary loss decays from `0.45` to `0.05` during base training to guide early branch learning while letting the fused classifier dominate later.\n]}
